$comment: Copied from spec/schemas/skill.spec.schema.json in microsoft/azure-sql-skills-lab, which is the source. Sidecars point at this path so editors validate on save. validate-catalog.mjs checks every sidecar against it, so a stale copy fails the build here rather than drifting silently.
title: skill.spec.jsonc
description: Everything about a skill that the agent must NOT read. Sits beside SKILL.md. The eval reads this file; the agent never does. There is deliberately no `personas` key: the primitive is the domain, and a persona is a maintained selection over domain plus posture (spec/personas.yaml). A per-skill persona list would make every persona rename a 142-file edit.

$schema.description: Points at this schema so editors validate on save. Permitted explicitly because additionalProperties is false and every shipped sidecar carries one.

id.description: Equals the SKILL.md name and the containing directory name.

domain.description: One slug from spec/taxonomy.yaml. Also the parent directory under skills/. Stripped on install.

value.description: The value bar. A skill must pass at least one of the first four. `convenience-only` alone is a reject, enforced by rule VAL001 rather than by this schema, so the rejection message can explain itself.

correction.description: The wrong belief this skill overwrites, in at least one complete sentence. If you cannot state it, the skill is not ready. This is the rule most likely to be argued with, which is why it is checked rather than reviewed.

posture.description: Descriptive only. NEVER an authorization control: a persona changes what is installed, never what is permitted.

applies_to.description: Scope is fixed (rules SCP001 to SCP003). Managed Instance, Fabric SQL and SQL Server on VMs are not values here and never will be.

related.description: Must resolve to other catalog ids, checked in CI. On fan-out, any entry outside the copied subset is rewritten to a canonical catalog URL or dropped.

target.description: Which substrate lane 4 runs this against.

triggering.description: Evals before content. At least three scenarios including one negative control, so a skill is written against measured failures rather than imagined ones.

negative.description: Prompts this skill must NOT fire on. Without these, a broad description scores well and routes badly.
